content: The effects of antithrombin III may be altered by an unknown mechanism. It is recommended to avoid or use an alternative drug in such cases. 1. Apalutamide: This drug decreases the levels or effects of quinine by inducing the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Avoid or substitute another drug. If co-administration is necessary, evaluate for loss of therapeutic efficacy, adjust doses as per prescribing information, and monitor closely. 2. Apomorphine and Quinine: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Aprepitant: This drug increases the levels or effects of quinine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The significance of this interaction is unknown, so monitor closely. 4. Arformoterol and Quinine: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Quinine and Argatroban: Quinine increases the effects of argatroban through an unknown mechanism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 6. Aripiprazole and Quinine: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 7. Armodafinil: This drug decreases the levels or effects of quinine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The significance of this interaction is unknown, so monitor closely. 8. Arsenic Trioxide and Quinine: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Artemether and Quinine: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 10. Artemether/Lumefantrine and Quinine: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Monitor closely. Artemether/Lumefantrine also decreases the levels or effects of quinine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 11. Asenapine and Quinine: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Asenapine Transdermal and Quinine: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 13. Atazanavir: This drug increases the levels or effects of quinine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The significance of this interaction is unknown, so monitor closely. 14. Quinine and Atogepant: Quinine increases the levels or effects of atogepant by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Atomoxetine and Quinine: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 16. Quinine and Atracurium: Quinine increases the effects of atracurium through pharmacodynamic synergy, leading to a risk of respiratory depression. This combination is contraindicated. 17. Quinine and Avapritinib: Quinine increases the levels or effects of avapritinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Quinine and Axitinib: Quinine increases the levels of axitinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Azithromycin and Quinine: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Quinine and Bedaquiline: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely, including ECG monitoring. 21. Quinine and Bemiparin: Quinine increases the effects of bemiparin through an unknown mechanism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 22. Quinine and Berotralstat: Quinine increases the levels of berotralstat by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Berotralstat also increases the levels or effects of quinine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Adjust doses of narrow therapeutic index drugs when co-administered. 23. Quinine and Betrixaban: Quinine increases the levels of betrixaban by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Reduce the betrixaban dose to 80 mg once, followed by 40 mg daily if co-administered with a P-gp inhibitor. 24. Quinine and Bivalirudin: Quinine increases the effects of bivalirudin through an unknown mechanism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 25. Blinatumomab: This drug increases the levels of quinine by decreasing its metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. The highest risk of drug-drug interactions occurs during the first 9 days of the first cycle and the first 2 days of the second cycle. 26. Bosentan: This drug decreases the levels or effects of quinine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The significance of this interaction is unknown, so monitor closely. 27. Bosutinib and Quinine: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Bremelanotide: This drug decreases the levels or effects of quinine by slowing gastric emptying, potentially reducing the absorption of oral medications. Avoid use with oral drugs dependent on threshold concentrations for efficacy. 29. Quinine and Brexpiprazole: Quinine increases the levels or effects of brexpiprazole by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce the brexpiprazole dose if co-administered with moderate CYP2D6 and strong/moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 30. Brigatinib: This drug decreases the levels or effects of quinine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Monitor CYP3A4 substrate levels and adjust doses as needed. 31. Brodalumab: This drug may normalize CYP450 enzyme formation by reducing cytokine levels during chronic inflammation. Monitor therapeutic effects when initiating or discontinuing brodalumab in patients receiving CYP450 substrates. 32. Budesonide: This drug decreases the levels or effects of quinine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The significance of this interaction is unknown, so monitor closely. 33. Quinine and Bupivacaine Implant: Both drugs may increase each other's toxicity, potentially causing methemoglobinemia. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Buprenorphine and Quinine: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 35. Butabarbital: This drug decreases the levels or effects of quinine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 36. Capecitabine and Quinine: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Carbamazepine: This drug decreases the levels or effects of quinine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Cenobamate: This drug decreases the levels or effects of quinine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Increase the dose of CYP3A4 substrates as needed. 39. Quinine and Ceritinib: Quinine increases the levels of ceritinib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Both drugs also increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 40. Chloroquine and Quinine: Chloroquine increases the toxicity of quinine by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 41. Chlorpromazine and Quinine: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Cimetidine: This drug increases the levels or effects of quinine by competing for renal tubular clearance and affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Ciprofloxacin and Quinine: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Quinine and Cisatracurium: Quinine increases the effects of cisatracurium through pharmacodynamic synergy, leading to a risk of respiratory depression. This combination is contraindicated. 45. Citalopram and Quinine: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. ECG monitoring is recommended. 46. Clarithromycin and Quinine: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Clarithromycin also increases the levels or effects of quinine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Clomipramine and Quinine: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Clozapine and Quinine: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Cobicistat: This drug increases the levels or effects of quinine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 50. Quinine and Colchicine: Quinine increases the levels or effects of colchicine by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug.
